resources.string: A previous Wi-Fi Direct connection is still running. Reset it to connect.
Allow Nearby devices for TVPlay in the device’s app permissions.
Allow precise Location for TVPlay in the device’s app permissions.
Allow the connection permission to continue
Connect your iPhone with a USB cable
Could not start CarPlay. Return to TVPlay and check app permissions.
On your iPhone, open Settings → Bluetooth and pair with the TV. Then return to TVPlay and choose Connect phone.
The iPhone has not sent a picture since CarPlay started. Restart the iPhone (turn it off and on), then connect again.
The device couldn’t start CarPlay Wi-Fi. Check Wi-Fi and close other projection apps. Retrying…
This device cannot use the smaller size at this resolution. Using Default.
This device may not support wireless CarPlay. Try a USB connection.
Turn on Bluetooth in system settings to connect.
Turn on Wi-Fi in system settings to connect.
Use a USB data cable and unlock your iPhone.\nAllow Trust and CarPlay if your iPhone asks.
Your iPhone didn’t switch to wired CarPlay. Unlock it and reconnect the cable. On iOS 15 or earlier, update iOS or use wireless CarPlay.
This device cannot open VPN authorization. Return to TVPlay to check connection permissions or use wireless.
Your iPhone isn’t available. Unlock it and check Bluetooth.
This video can\'t play on the screen. Protected video, such as Apple TV+, needs a licensed receiver.
Timed out waiting for the hotspot. Open the hotspot in system settings.
The device could not start its hotspot. Open the hotspot in system settings.
Touch and hold the report text to select and copy it. You can use this if no sharing app is available.
The iPhone did not connect to CarPlay in time
Automatic retries stopped. Check the connection and retry manually.

This device’s Android Bluetooth reports a connection, but nothing reaches the iPhone: even a connection to a service that does not exist succeeds. Bluetooth here is handled by the maker’s own module, which apps cannot use, so wireless CarPlay cannot work on this device. Try a USB connection.
This device’s Android Bluetooth cannot open connections for apps: its firmware leaves out the part that apps connect through. Wireless CarPlay cannot work on this device. Try a USB connection.
An old Wi-Fi Direct group may block this connection. Select Reset CarPlay Wi-Fi below, then connect again.
This device cannot send Bluetooth data to the iPhone. Wireless CarPlay cannot work here. Use a USB data cable.
Turn the hotspot off and retry, or choose Built-in hotspot in Connection setup and save its name and password.
The hotspot is on, and Wi-Fi Direct cannot start beside it
The iPhone chosen in TVPlay is no longer paired with the device
Pair the iPhone with Bluetooth again, or return to TVPlay and choose another iPhone. Then retry.
Several devices are paired. Return to TVPlay, choose your iPhone, then retry.
Wi-Fi Direct cannot use the preferred channel
Set Preferred Wi-Fi Direct channel to Auto in Connection setup, then retry.
The device doesn\'t see any USB device yet
The device sees a USB device, but not an iPhone
Use a USB data cable (some cables only charge), plug it into the USB data port, and unlock the iPhone.
Use a USB data cable in the USB data port, unplug other USB devices, and unlock the iPhone.
The hotspot settings differ from those saved in TVPlay
In Connection setup, copy the name and password from the system hotspot settings, then retry.
The hotspot interface saved in TVPlay does not exist on this device
In Connection setup, clear Hotspot interface (optional), then retry.
Turn on the hotspot in system settings, then retry.
Check that the hotspot is on and its name and password match TVPlay settings. If available, use 5 GHz, then retry.
Keep Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. On the iPhone, join the hotspot and enable Auto-Join, then retry. Save a diagnostic report if it still fails.
Allow the requested USB, Nearby devices or Location permissions for TVPlay on the device, then retry.
Use a USB data port and a data-capable cable. Unlock the iPhone, approve Trust and CarPlay, then retry.
Unlock the iPhone, enable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and pair it with the device. Keep it nearby, then retry.
Retry the connection. If it fails again, return to TVPlay and save a diagnostic report.
Keep the device\'s Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on and the iPhone unlocked nearby, then retry. If it keeps failing, forget the receiver on the iPhone under Settings → General → CarPlay and connect again.
Make sure the device and the iPhone are on the same Wi-Fi network and its name and password match TVPlay settings, then retry.
Turn on Bluetooth before starting wireless CarPlay.
Permissions are required to start CarPlay.
